title: Fair Payment Terms
content: Client shall pay Consultant the fees set forth in Exhibit A within thirty (30) days of receipt of an accurate and undisputed invoice. In the event of a bona fide dispute regarding any invoice, Client shall pay the undisputed portion when due and the parties shall work in good faith to resolve the disputed portion within fifteen (15) business days. Late payments shall accrue simple interest at the lesser of 1% per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law.

title: Fair Termination Clause
content: Either party may terminate this Agreement (a) for material breach by the other party that remains uncured for thirty (30) days after written notice, or (b) upon sixty (60) days written notice for convenience. Upon termination, Consultant shall be paid for all work completed through the effective date of termination plus any non-cancellable expenses incurred. All provisions that by their nature should survive termination, including confidentiality, limitation of liability, and payment obligations, shall so survive.

title: Balanced Limitation of Liability
content: Neither party shall be liable for any indirect, incidental, special, or consequential damages arising out of or related to this Agreement, including lost profits, except in cases of gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, or breach of confidentiality obligations. Each party's total aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the total fees paid or payable under this Agreement during the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, or (b) one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000). These limitations shall not apply to indemnification obligations, breach of confidentiality, or infringement of intellectual property rights.

title: Mutual Confidentiality Clause
content: Each party (the 'Receiving Party') agrees to hold in strict confidence all non-public information disclosed by the other party (the 'Disclosing Party'), whether in writing, orally, or through any other medium, that is clearly identified as confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential (collectively, 'Confidential Information'). The Receiving Party shall use at least the same degree of care as it uses with its own similar confidential information, but in no event less than reasonable care. Confidential Information excludes information that (a) is or becomes publicly available through no breach, (b) was lawfully known prior to disclosure, (c) is independently developed without use of Confidential Information, or (d) is required to be disclosed by law, provided the Receiving Party gives prompt notice and reasonable cooperation to limit such disclosure.

title: Balanced IP Ownership
content: Consultant retains all right, title, and interest in its pre-existing materials, tools, methodologies, and know-how ('Consultant IP'). Upon full payment, Consultant assigns to Client all right, title, and interest in the deliverables specifically created for Client under this Agreement ('Work Product'), excluding Consultant IP. Consultant grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, worldwide license to use any Consultant IP incorporated into the Work Product solely to the extent necessary for Client to use the Work Product. Each party represents that its contributions will not infringe the intellectual property rights of any third party.

title: Fair Data Processing Clause
content: Each party shall comply with all applicable data protection laws, including the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), as applicable. Consultant shall process personal data only on documented instructions from Client and shall implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal data against unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction. Consultant shall notify Client of any data breach involving Client's personal data within forty-eight (48) hours of discovery. Consultant shall not sell, retain, or use Client's personal data for any purpose other than performing the Services under this Agreement.

title: Reasonable Non-Solicitation
content: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of twelve (12) months thereafter, each party agrees not to solicit for employment or hire any employee of the other party who was materially involved in the performance of this Agreement, provided that this restriction shall not apply to general public solicitations not targeted at such employees. The parties agree that this restriction is reasonable in scope and duration and is necessary to protect the legitimate business interests of each party. Nothing in this clause shall restrict a party from engaging in its ordinary course of business or serving any client or customer.

title: Fair Dispute Resolution
content: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. Before initiating any formal legal proceedings, the parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute through good-faith negotiation for a period of thirty (30) days. If negotiation fails, the parties shall submit the dispute to non-binding mediation administered by a mutually agreed mediator, with costs shared equally. Any litigation shall be brought exclusively in the state or federal courts located in the agreed venue, and each party irrevocably consents to such jurisdiction and waives any objection to venue.

title: Fair Force Majeure Provision
content: Neither party shall be liable for any delay or failure to perform its obligations under this Agreement to the extent such delay or failure results from causes beyond its reasonable control, including acts of God, war, terrorism, civil unrest, epidemic, pandemic, fire, flood, earthquake, governmental action, or failure of utilities or telecommunications networks (each a 'Force Majeure Event'). The affected party shall (a) promptly notify the other party of the Force Majeure Event, its expected duration, and the obligations affected, and (b) use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate the impact and resume performance. If a Force Majeure Event continues for more than thirty (30) days, either party may terminate this Agreement without liability upon written notice.

title: Balanced Warranty Terms
content: Consultant warrants that (a) the Services shall be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards, (b) Consultant has the full right and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement, and (c) the Work Product, when delivered, shall materially conform to the specifications set forth in the applicable statement of work. EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED HEREIN, THE SERVICES AND WORK PRODUCT ARE PROVIDED 'AS IS,' AND CONSULTANT DISCLAIMS ALL IMPLIED WARRANTIES, INCLUDING MERCHANTABILITY AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. Client warrants that it has the authority to grant Consultant access to any Client systems or data necessary to perform the Services.

title: Fair Employee Notice Period
content: The Employee shall provide thirty (30) days written notice to the Employer prior to resignation. The Employer may, at its sole discretion, waive the notice period in whole or in part or provide pay in lieu of notice calculated at the Employee's base salary rate. During the notice period, the Employee shall continue to perform their duties and cooperate in the orderly transition of responsibilities. The Employer shall not withhold termination documents, relieving letters, or final settlement on account of the notice period if the Employee has completed at least fifteen (15) days of active service during the notice period.

title: Fair Employer Termination Procedure
content: The Employer may terminate this Agreement for cause immediately upon written notice in cases of gross misconduct, fraud, willful insubordination, or material breach of employment terms. For performance-related termination, the Employer shall (a) provide a written warning specifying the performance deficiencies, (b) allow the Employee a reasonable improvement period of not less than thirty (30) days, and (c) provide reasonable support and feedback during the improvement period. Termination without cause shall require thirty (30) days written notice or pay in lieu of notice. In all cases, the Employee shall receive a written statement of reasons for termination.

title: Fair Employee Transfer Policy
content: The Employer may transfer the Employee to an alternative location or role upon providing at least fifteen (15) days written notice. For transfers exceeding fifty (50) kilometers from the current work location, the Employer shall provide a reasonable relocation allowance covering moving expenses and temporary accommodation for up to seven (7) days. The Employee has the right to decline a transfer on valid grounds including proven medical hardship, caregiving responsibilities for immediate family members, or lack of comparable facilities at the new location for dependents with special needs. No adverse action shall be taken against an Employee who reasonably declines a transfer.

title: Fair Employee Gratuity Terms
content: The Employer shall pay gratuity to the Employee in accordance with the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, or applicable local law, whichever is more favorable to the Employee. Gratuity shall be calculated at fifteen (15) days wages for each completed year of service, based on the last drawn basic salary plus dearness allowance. Payment of gratuity shall be made within thirty (30) days of the Employee's last working day, regardless of the reason for separation. Gratuity payment shall not be conditioned upon the Employer receiving payment from any client, customer, or third party. Interest at 10% per annum shall accrue on delayed gratuity payments beyond the thirty-day period.

title: Fair Employee Confidentiality Clause
content: The Employee shall maintain the confidentiality of all proprietary and trade secret information of the Employer for a period of two (2) years following termination of employment. Confidential Information does not include information that (a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the Employee, (b) was known to the Employee prior to employment as evidenced by written records, or (c) the Employee is required to disclose by law, court order, or governmental authority. Nothing in this clause shall prevent the Employee from reporting suspected violations of law to any government agency, making protected whistleblower disclosures, or cooperating in any government investigation.

title: Fair Employee Non-Compete Clause
content: During employment and for a period of six (6) months following termination, the Employee shall not directly or indirectly engage in any business that is in direct competition with the Employer's core business within the same geographic territory where the Employee performed services. During the restricted period, the Employer shall pay the Employee compensation equal to fifty percent (50%) of the Employee's last drawn monthly base salary, paid monthly in arrears. The non-compete restriction shall apply only to competitors specifically identified in the employment letter, not to all businesses in the Employer's industry. This clause shall not restrict the Employee from accepting employment with a non-competitor or in a different business vertical.

title: Fair Employee IP Assignment
content: The Employee agrees to assign to the Employer all inventions, discoveries, improvements, and works of authorship created within the scope of employment and using the Employer's resources during working hours ('Work Product'). The Employee retains full ownership of any intellectual property (a) developed entirely on the Employee's own time, (b) without the use of the Employer's equipment, supplies, facilities, or trade secret information, and (c) that does not relate to the Employer's business or actual or anticipated research. The Employer shall not claim ownership over the Employee's pre-existing intellectual property unless such IP is specifically contributed to a project as documented in writing.

title: Fair Employee Indemnity Clause
content: The Employer agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the Employee against all claims, liabilities, losses, damages, and reasonable legal expenses arising from the Employee's performance of duties within the scope of employment, except where such claims result from the Employee's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud. The Employee's obligation to indemnify the Employer is limited to cases of proven gross negligence or willful misconduct and shall not exceed the greater of (a) three (3) months of the Employee's base salary, or (b) the amount covered under the Employer's applicable insurance policy. The Employer shall maintain adequate directors and officers or professional liability insurance covering employees.

title: Fair Employee Salary Payment Terms
content: The Employer shall pay the Employee's monthly salary on or before the seventh (7th) day of each calendar month. Salary shall be paid via electronic bank transfer to the Employee's designated bank account. The Employer shall provide the Employee with a detailed written salary statement showing gross salary, all deductions (tax, provident fund, professional tax, insurance), and net salary paid. Any unauthorized deduction from salary is prohibited. In the event of salary payment delay exceeding seven (7) calendar days, simple interest at the rate of 1% per month shall accrue on the outstanding amount from the due date until payment is made. Interest on delayed salary shall be paid along with the next month's salary.

title: Fair Employee Working Hours Clause
content: The Employee's normal working hours shall not exceed forty-eight (48) hours per week, with a maximum of nine (9) hours per day exclusive of rest intervals. The Employee shall be entitled to a rest break of at least thirty (30) minutes after every five (5) hours of continuous work. Any work performed beyond the normal working hours shall be treated as overtime and compensated at twice (2x) the Employee's regular hourly rate. Overtime shall be voluntary and not mandatory. The Employee is entitled to one (1) full rest day per week, typically Sunday. The total overtime hours in any quarter shall not exceed one hundred twenty-five (125) hours. The Employer shall maintain accurate records of all hours worked and overtime paid.

title: Fair Supplier Payment Terms
content: Buyer shall pay Supplier the invoiced amount within thirty (30) days of receipt of Goods Receipt Note (GRN), inspection acceptance, and a valid tax invoice, whichever is later. Supplier shall submit invoices with GSTIN, HSN code, PO reference, and supporting documents as specified in the Purchase Order. Retention money of five percent (5%) of each invoice shall be withheld until successful completion of all delivery obligations and expiry of the defect liability period. Retention shall be released within thirty (30) days of DLP completion certificate issuance. Late payments beyond the thirty-day credit period shall accrue simple interest at the rate of one percent (1%) per month on the outstanding amount.

title: Fair Supplier Delivery Terms
content: Supplier shall deliver all goods Delivered Duty Paid (DDP) to Buyer's designated site as per Incoterms 2020. Risk of loss or damage shall transfer to Buyer only upon delivery and acceptance at the designated site. Delivery shall be in accordance with the delivery schedule set forth in the Purchase Order. Supplier shall notify Buyer of dispatch at least seven (7) days in advance. In the event of delay attributable to Supplier, liquidated damages at the rate of zero point five percent (0.5%) of the delayed item value per week of delay shall apply, capped at ten percent (10%) of the total Purchase Order value. Buyer may cancel the order if delay exceeds eight (8) weeks without prejudice to other remedies.

title: Fair Supplier Pricing Clause
content: All prices set forth in the Purchase Order are firm and fixed for a period of twelve (12) months from the Effective Date of this Agreement. Any price revision thereafter shall require mutual written agreement and shall not exceed the change in the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) plus two percent (2%) per annum, calculated on a compounded basis. Supplier shall provide sixty (60) days advance written notice of any proposed price revision along with supporting documentation justifying the increase. Buyer reserves the right to source from alternative suppliers if the revised price exceeds prevailing market rates by more than ten percent (10%). No retroactive price adjustments shall apply.

title: Fair Supplier Quality Standards
content: All goods supplied shall conform to ISO 9001:2015 quality management standards and any additional specifications referenced in the Purchase Order. Supplier shall conduct Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) at its premises in accordance with an agreed Inspection and Test Plan (ITP) identifying hold points, witness points, and review points. Buyer or its nominated third-party inspection agency shall have the right to witness all hold points. Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) shall be conducted at Buyer's site within fourteen (14) days of delivery. Supplier shall provide material test certificates, calibration certificates, and certificates of conformance for each batch. Goods not conforming to specifications may be rejected within thirty (30) days of delivery.

title: Fair Supplier Warranty Terms
content: Supplier warrants that all goods supplied shall be free from defects in material and workmanship for a period of twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning or twenty-seven (27) months from the date of delivery, whichever occurs first. During the warranty period, Supplier shall, at Buyer's option, repair or replace any defective goods at Supplier's sole cost and expense. Supplier shall respond to warranty claims within forty-eight (48) hours for critical defects affecting operations and within seven (7) calendar days for non-critical defects. If Supplier fails to remedy a critical defect within fourteen (14) days, Buyer may engage a third party at Supplier's cost. The warranty excludes consumable items, normal wear and tear, and damage caused by Buyer's misuse.

title: Fair Supplier Defect Liability Period
content: A Defect Liability Period (DLP) of twelve (12) months shall apply from the date of Site Acceptance Testing completion. During the DLP, Supplier shall rectify any defect attributable to faulty design, materials, or workmanship at its own cost within fourteen (14) calendar days of written notice from Buyer. For emergency defects affecting safety or operations, Supplier shall respond within forty-eight (48) hours and complete rectification within seven (7) days. If Supplier fails to rectify within the specified timeline, Buyer may engage a third party at Supplier's reasonable cost. The retention money of five percent (5%) shall be released within thirty (30) days of issuance of the DLP completion certificate confirming all defects have been satisfactorily rectified.

title: Balanced Supplier Liability Clause
content: Each party's total aggregate liability to the other under or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed one hundred percent (100%) of the total Purchase Order value. Neither party shall be liable for any indirect, incidental, special, or consequential damages including loss of profit, loss of revenue, or loss of production. The limitations of liability shall not apply to (a) death or personal injury caused by negligence, (b) fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, (c) gross negligence or willful misconduct, (d) breach of confidentiality obligations, or (e) infringement of third-party intellectual property rights. Each party shall maintain adequate insurance to cover its potential liability under this Agreement.

title: Fair Supplier Indemnity Clause
content: Each party (the 'Indemnifying Party') shall indemnify and hold harmless the other party (the 'Indemnified Party') against all claims, losses, and reasonable legal costs arising from (a) death or personal injury caused by the Indemnifying Party's negligence, (b) damage to tangible property caused by the Indemnifying Party, and (c) infringement of third-party intellectual property rights by goods or materials provided by the Indemnifying Party. The Indemnified Party shall promptly notify the Indemnifying Party of any claim, allow the Indemnifying Party to conduct the defense, and provide reasonable cooperation. The indemnity shall be limited to the liability cap set forth in the Limitation of Liability clause.

title: Fair Supplier Termination Clause
content: Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by providing ninety (90) days written notice to the other party. Either party may terminate immediately for material breach that remains uncured for thirty (30) days after written notice. Upon termination, Supplier shall (a) deliver all completed goods and work-in-progress for which Buyer has paid, (b) return all Buyer-owned materials, tools, and confidential information within fifteen (15) days, and (c) provide reasonable transition assistance for up to thirty (30) days. Buyer shall pay for all goods completed and accepted before termination plus the reasonable cost of materials specifically procured for this Agreement that cannot be mitigated. All outstanding invoices shall be settled within forty-five (45) days of termination.

title: Fair Supplier Force Majeure Clause
content: Neither party shall be liable for delay or failure to perform due to Force Majeure Events including acts of God, war, terrorism, civil unrest, epidemic, pandemic, cyber attack, fire, flood, earthquake, governmental action, or failure of utilities or telecommunications networks. The affected party shall notify the other within seven (7) days of the Force Majeure Event, describing its impact and expected duration. Both parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate the effects. If a Force Majeure Event continues for more than ninety (90) days, either party may terminate this Agreement without liability by providing thirty (30) days written notice. Supplier shall refund any advance payment for goods not delivered due to the Force Majeure Event.

title: Fair Supplier Confidentiality Clause
content: Each party shall protect the other's Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care as it uses for its own similar information, but not less than reasonable care. The confidentiality obligation shall survive for three (3) years after termination or expiry of this Agreement. Confidential Information excludes information that (a) is or becomes publicly available without breach, (b) was lawfully known prior to disclosure without confidentiality restriction, (c) is independently developed without use of the Confidential Information, or (d) is required to be disclosed by law, court order, or regulatory authority. Upon termination, each party shall return or destroy all Confidential Information of the other party within thirty (30) days and provide a written certificate of destruction.

title: Fair Supplier Intellectual Property Clause
content: All intellectual property rights in goods, designs, software, or documentation specifically created for Buyer under this Agreement ('Foreground IP') shall vest in and be owned exclusively by Buyer upon full payment. Supplier retains all right, title, and interest in its pre-existing intellectual property, tools, methodologies, and know-how ('Supplier Background IP'). Supplier grants Buyer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, worldwide, non-exclusive license to use Supplier Background IP to the extent necessary for Buyer to use, maintain, and modify the goods delivered under this Agreement. Each party warrants that its contributions shall not infringe the intellectual property rights of any third party and shall indemnify the other against any such infringement claims.

title: Fair Supplier Insurance Clause
content: Supplier shall maintain at its own cost the following insurance coverage: (a) General Liability insurance of not less than INR 1 Crore per occurrence, (b) Product Liability insurance of not less than INR 50 Lakhs per occurrence, (c) Workers' Compensation insurance as required by applicable law, and (d) Transit Insurance for full replacement value of all goods in transit. Supplier shall provide annual certificates of insurance to Buyer naming Buyer as an additional insured. Coverage shall be with reputable insurers having a minimum credit rating of A-. Supplier shall notify Buyer within seven (7) days of any material change to or cancellation of insurance coverage. Failure to maintain insurance shall constitute a material breach.

title: Fair Supplier Order Management
content: Supplier shall acknowledge each Purchase Order within five (5) business days of receipt. The acknowledgment shall confirm delivery date, price, and any deviations from the Purchase Order terms. Any discrepancy between the Purchase Order and Supplier's acknowledgment must be raised within three (3) business days; failure to raise a discrepancy shall constitute acceptance of the Purchase Order terms. Supplier shall provide order status updates weekly and notify Buyer immediately of any anticipated delay. Buyer may amend or cancel a Purchase Order without charge if Supplier has not commenced procurement or manufacturing. For customized goods, cancellation charges shall be limited to Supplier's demonstrable, non-recoverable costs.

title: Fair Supplier Compliance Clause
content: Supplier shall comply with all applicable laws including the Goods and Services Tax Act, labour laws, environmental regulations, and anti-bribery legislation including the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act. Supplier shall issue valid GST-compliant tax invoices with correct HSN codes, GSTIN, and place of supply. Supplier represents that it has not and shall not offer any bribe, kickback, or improper payment to any Buyer employee or government official. Supplier shall comply with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act) in handling any personal data of Buyer's employees or customers. Breach of this compliance clause shall constitute grounds for immediate termination.

title: Fair Works Contract Payment Terms
content: Contractor shall submit monthly Running Account (RA) bills based on measured quantities of work executed, supported by measurement sheets and supporting documents. The Employer's Engineer shall certify the RA bill within fourteen (14) calendar days of submission. The Employer shall pay the certified amount within thirty (30) days of certification, less retention money of five percent (5%). Retention shall be released in two stages: fifty percent (50%) upon issuance of the Practical Completion Certificate and the remaining fifty percent (50%) upon issuance of the Final Completion Certificate or expiry of the Defect Liability Period, whichever is later. Advance payment of ten percent (10%) of contract value shall be made against an unconditional Bank Guarantee of equivalent amount.

title: Fair Works Contract Variation Procedure
content: All variations to the Scope of Work shall be instructed through a written Variation Order (VO) signed by both parties. Upon receiving a VO request, the Contractor shall submit a cost and time impact assessment within fourteen (14) calendar days. The parties shall mutually agree on the cost and time adjustment before the variation work commences. Where agreement cannot be reached, the variation shall be valued using the contract rates or, if no applicable rates exist, fair market rates plus a reasonable allowance for overhead and profit. The cumulative value of all variations shall not exceed fifteen percent (15%) of the original contract value without a formal contract amendment. Any variation shall automatically entitle the Contractor to a proportionate extension of time.

title: Fair Works Contract Extension of Time
content: The Contractor shall be entitled to an Extension of Time (EOT) for completion for any delay caused by (a) Employer-caused delays including late site possession, late drawing approvals, or late supply of Employer-provided materials, (b) variations instructed under the Variation clause, (c) Force Majeure Events, (d) exceptionally adverse weather conditions exceeding ten-year averages, (e) material shortages beyond the Contractor's control, (f) statutory changes, or (g) concurrent delay where the Employer is partially responsible. The Contractor shall notify the Engineer within twenty-eight (28) days of the event giving rise to the EOT claim. EOT shall be assessed by the Engineer within twenty-eight (28) days of submission. Employer-caused delays shall additionally entitle the Contractor to cost relief for prolongation and disruption.

title: Fair Works Contract Milestone & LDs
content: The Contractor shall achieve the milestones set forth in the Milestone Schedule attached as an Annexure. Sectional completion shall be permitted for distinct parts of the Works capable of independent use. Delay liquidated damages for failure to achieve a milestone by the scheduled date shall be zero point one percent (0.1%) of the affected section value per day of delay, capped at ten percent (10%) of the total contract value. Liquidated damages shall be the Employer's sole remedy for delay, excluding termination for prolonged default. No liquidated damages shall apply for delays caused by Employer's default, variations, or Force Majeure Events. An early completion bonus of fifty percent (50%) of the LD rate per day shall be payable for each day of early completion, capped at five percent (5%) of contract value.

title: Fair Works Contract Quality Standards
content: The Contractor shall implement a Quality Assurance Plan in accordance with ISO 9001:2015. An Inspection and Test Plan (ITP) shall be submitted for approval within thirty (30) days of commencement, identifying all Hold Points (H), Witness Points (W), and Review Points (R). The Employer's Engineer or a nominated third-party inspection agency shall witness all Hold Points before the Contractor may proceed. Material submittals including samples, catalogues, and test certificates shall be submitted for approval fourteen (14) days before procurement. Work covered without inspection at a Hold Point shall be uncovered at the Contractor's cost for inspection. Non-conforming work shall be rectified or re-executed at the Contractor's cost to meet specifications.

title: Fair Works Contract Materials Clause
content: Employer-supplied materials shall be delivered to the Site in accordance with the delivery schedule set forth in the Materials Schedule annexure. Delays in delivery of Employer-supplied materials shall entitle the Contractor to an Extension of Time and cost relief for standing time and prolongation. The Contractor shall inspect Employer-supplied materials within seven (7) days of delivery and notify the Employer of any defects or shortages. Materials supplied by the Contractor shall be subject to the approval process defined in the ITP. The Contractor shall provide secure storage for all materials on Site and maintain an inventory register. Materials incorporated into the Works shall become the property of the Employer upon payment.

title: Fair Works Contract Defect Liability Period
content: A Defect Liability Period (DLP) of twelve (12) months shall commence from the date of Practical Completion for non-structural works and twenty-four (24) months for structural works. The Contractor shall rectify any defect notified during the DLP within fourteen (14) calendar days, or seven (7) days for emergency defects affecting safety or operations. If the Contractor fails to rectify within the specified period, the Employer may engage others at the Contractor's cost. The retention money shall be released only after issuance of the DLP completion certificate confirming all defects have been satisfactorily rectified. The Contractor's liability for latent structural defects shall survive for a period of five (5) years from Practical Completion.

title: Fair Works Performance Security
content: The Contractor shall provide an unconditional, on-demand Performance Bank Guarantee for ten percent (10%) of the contract value from a scheduled bank acceptable to the Employer. The Performance Security shall be valid until Final Completion plus six (6) months. The Employer may reduce the Performance Security to five percent (5%) upon issuance of the Practical Completion Certificate, subject to satisfactory progress and no outstanding claims. The Employer shall release the Performance Security within thirty (30) days of Final Completion. An advance payment guarantee for one hundred percent (100%) of the advance amount shall be provided separately and shall be released proportionally as the advance is recovered through running bills.

title: Fair Works Contract Insurance Requirements
content: The Contractor shall maintain at its own cost: (a) Contractors All Risk (CAR) / Erection All Risk (EAR) insurance for not less than one hundred ten percent (110%) of the contract value covering all risks of physical loss or damage to the Works, (b) Third-Party Liability insurance of INR 5 Crore per occurrence, (c) Workers' Compensation insurance as required by the Employees' Compensation Act, (d) Professional Indemnity insurance of INR 2 Crore if the Contractor has design responsibility, and (e) Motor Vehicle and Plant & Equipment insurance. The Employer shall be named as co-insured on the CAR/EAR and Third-Party Liability policies. Insurance certificates shall be submitted before commencement and renewed annually.

title: Fair Works Contract Claims Procedure
content: The Contractor shall give notice of any claim for additional payment or time within twenty-eight (28) days of the event giving rise to the claim. The notice shall describe the event, its impact on cost and time, and the contractual basis for the claim. The Contractor shall submit a fully detailed claim with supporting documentation within forty-two (42) days of the event. The Engineer shall determine the claim within forty-two (42) days of receipt of the fully detailed submission. If the Contractor disagrees with the Engineer's determination, the matter shall be referred to a Dispute Adjudication Board (DAB) comprising one or three members appointed by mutual agreement. The DAB shall give its decision within eighty-four (84) days of referral. Loss and expense claims shall include prolongation costs, disruption costs, and head-office overheads calculated using agreed formula or actual audited costs.

title: Fair Works Contract Termination Clause
content: Either party may terminate this Contract for convenience upon ninety (90) days written notice. The Employer may terminate immediately for Contractor default including (a) abandonment of the Works, (b) persistent failure to proceed with due diligence, (c) subcontracting without consent, or (d) material breach of safety or environmental obligations. The Contractor may terminate immediately for Employer default including (a) failure to pay certified amounts within sixty (60) days, (b) failure to provide site possession for more than ninety (90) days, or (c) suspension of the Works for more than one hundred eighty (180) days. Upon termination, the Contractor shall be paid for work executed, materials ordered, demobilization costs, and loss of profit on the unexecuted portion at five percent (5%) of the remaining contract value.

title: Fair Works Contract HSE Requirements
content: The Contractor shall submit a Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) Plan within fourteen (14) days of commencement, compliant with the National Building Code (NBC) 2016, the Factories Act, and applicable environmental regulations. The Contractor shall appoint a dedicated HSE Officer and conduct daily toolbox talks and weekly safety audits. All personnel shall undergo site safety induction before commencing work. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) shall be provided to all workers at the Contractor's cost. Accidents resulting in lost time injury shall be reported within four (4) hours and investigated within forty-eight (48) hours. The Contractor shall maintain a valid environmental clearance and consent to operate. Monthly HSE performance reports shall be submitted including leading and lagging indicators.

title: Fair Works Contract Subcontracting
content: The Contractor may subcontract portions of the Works with the prior written consent of the Employer, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. Consent shall not be required for subcontracts valued below five percent (5%) of the contract value. The Contractor shall remain fully liable for all subcontractor work as if it were performed by the Contractor itself. All subcontracts shall include back-to-back provisions equivalent to the terms of this Contract. The Contractor shall submit a list of proposed subcontractors and their scope of work for approval. The Employer shall have the right to audit subcontractor quality, safety, and financial standing. Nominated subcontractors selected by the Employer shall not relieve the Contractor of coordination and interface responsibility.

title: Fair Works Contract Dispute Resolution
content: All disputes shall be resolved through a tiered process: (a) negotiation between the Contractor's Project Manager and the Employer's Engineer within fourteen (14) days of the dispute notice, (b) if unresolved, negotiation between senior management of both parties within a further fourteen (14) days, (c) if still unresolved, non-binding mediation by a mutually agreed mediator within thirty (30) days, and (d) finally, binding arbitration under the rules of the Indian Council of Arbitration (ICA) or Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) as agreed. The arbitration seat shall be in India, conducted in English, with a sole arbitrator for claims below INR 1 Crore and a three-member tribunal for larger claims. The losing party shall bear the arbitration costs. The courts at the seat shall have exclusive supervisory jurisdiction.

title: Fair Works Contract Scope Definition
content: The Scope of Work is exhaustively defined in Annexure A — Bill of Quantities (BOQ), Annexure B — Technical Specifications, Annexure C — Drawings, and Annexure D — Work Exclusions. Any work not described in these annexures is expressly excluded from the Contract. The BOQ quantities are approximate and subject to re-measurement; the Contractor shall be paid for actual quantities executed at the agreed unit rates. The Contractor shall execute the Works in accordance with the latest revision of drawings issued for construction.
